title: Parisian Room, Almerocka and the Cincinnati and Ohio trips
summary: The band plays the Parisian Room and Almerocka, gets Look magazine coverage, and is taken to Cincinnati, Ohio and Indiana; a record is made in Ohio and another in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: The Parisian Room, yeah. Yeah, the Parisian Room. Well, we played there one Saturday night, and the Almerocka Club had warned us. So, after we got through playing there was this fellow, Eddie Kidd Wolf, former friend, a dry spider, and his partner was named Frank. He was an Italian. Well, when we got through playing at the Parisian Room, we went there and finished out the night, because we knocked off at 12 o'clock at the Parisian Room. And we went there and played a couple hours until 2 o'clock in the morning. Well, they hired us to play every night. Well, we played there for over a year. And that's where this big blow-up of this band got recognition in the Look magazine. I guess you remember that. Well, we started traveling, and at that time when we was playing there, Reverend Kershaw and his wife and Professor Ball of the University of Cincinnati was down here for a band. Well, they started from Myrtleville in Boivin, where we was playing there, Almerocka, and went down in every place that had a band. And they selected us. Well, when we went to Cincinnati, we made a tape for the archives of the University of Cincinnati. Well, after we made that tape, we played a concert for the University of Cincinnati. And we left there and went into Oxford, Ohio. And after that, they started bringing us out there regularly. We started going into Bloomington. We went into Bloomington, Indiana. We went to, uh, oh. Well, anyway, we covered a lot of territory in Ohio. Then we started traveling to California. We started alternating in California between, uh, Los Angeles and San Francisco. See? We played three months at the Beverly Cavern, and played three months for Doc at the Hangover in San Francisco. Doc, who? All I knew was Doc. That's what we used to call him, you know, Doc. Well, anyhow, after we wound up there, we went to start working at the Tin Angel. That was on Embarcadera. Embarcadera, and, oh, I can't think of the name. It's simple, too. But anyhow, we started working there every night. That was around 50, or the part of 57. Well, at that time they wanted George Lewis band in England, but he had to make an appearance face over there. Well, he left the band in my charge, and mistake taking him over to England.

Yeah, that was in 57. Well, he made several, uh, he made a tour of England. And, uh, when he came back, we were still in Frisco. We made a recording. I think it was Empirical. It's a red record. You may have that record.
The Empirical record was the one made in Ohio.
That was the one made in Ohio. Well, we made a red record on Powell Street in San Francisco. I can't think of the name of that company. We had Tom Jefferson on trumpet.
